definition: Ready to face and deal with danger or pain; showing courage.
exampleSentences: The brave knight protected the village from the dragon.
She was brave enough to speak in front of the whole school.
tip: Think of a superhero — they are always brave!

definition: To find or learn something for the first time.
exampleSentences: The explorer went on a journey to discover new lands.
I discovered a hidden path in the forest behind our house.
tip: Dis-COVER means to take the cover off something hidden!

definition: Very large in size, quantity, or extent.
exampleSentences: The elephant was enormous compared to the tiny mouse.
We saw an enormous rainbow stretching across the sky.
tip: E-NOR-MOUS — it's so big it needs a big word!

definition: Feeling or showing thanks for something.
exampleSentences: I am grateful for my wonderful family.
The lost puppy looked grateful when we gave it food and water.
tip: GRATE-ful — a great feeling of being thankful!

exampleSentences: It is important to brush your teeth every day.
The teacher shared an important message about kindness.
tip: If something is important, it IMPORTS meaning into your life!

definition: A long trip from one place to another.
exampleSentences: The family set out on a journey across the country.
Learning to read is a wonderful journey.
tip: Every journey starts with a single step!

definition: To make something clear and easy to understand.
exampleSentences: Can you explain how to solve this math problem?
The scientist explained why the sky is blue.
tip: When you explain, you make the plain truth clear!

definition: To make or bring something new into existence.
exampleSentences: Artists create beautiful paintings with colors and brushes.
We worked together to create a poster for the science fair.
tip: When you CREATE, you make something GREAT!

definition: Free from noise, worry, or conflict; calm and quiet.
exampleSentences: The peaceful lake reflected the mountains like a mirror.
After the storm, the night became peaceful and still.

definition: To make something better than it was before.
exampleSentences: Practice helps you improve your handwriting.
The town improved the park by adding new swings and slides.
tip: IM-PROVE — prove that you can do better!

exampleSentences: She had a brilliant idea for the school project.
The brilliant stars lit up the night sky.
tip: Brilliant things shine bright like a diamond!

definition: To feel sure that something is true or real.
exampleSentences: I believe we can finish this puzzle together.
Do you believe that practice makes perfect?
tip: BE-LIEVE — you have to BE something to achieve!

definition: To watch something carefully and closely.
exampleSentences: Scientists observe animals in their natural habitats.
I like to observe the clouds and imagine shapes.
tip: Good writers OBSERVE the world around them!

definition: Causing great surprise or wonder; wonderful.
exampleSentences: The magician performed an amazing trick.
It was amazing to see dolphins swimming alongside our boat.
tip: Something amazing puts you in A MAZE of wonder!

definition: Having made a firm decision and not willing to give up.
exampleSentences: The determined climber reached the top of the mountain.
She was determined to learn how to ride a bicycle.
tip: When you're determined, nothing can stop you!

definition: To put forward an idea for others to think about.
exampleSentences: I suggest we go to the library after school.
The teacher suggested reading the book before the test.
tip: When you suggest, you JEST (offer) an idea!

definition: An exciting or unusual experience or activity.
exampleSentences: Reading books takes you on incredible adventures.
Going camping in the woods was a real adventure.
tip: Every day can be an adventure if you look for one!

definition: A group of people living in the same area or sharing common interests.
exampleSentences: Our community came together to clean up the park.
The school is an important part of our community.
tip: COMM-UNITY — people coming together in UNITY!
